name: MiniCPM-OCR Jev

lineage.how_derived: language-model head replaced with a binary classification head that learns whether a candidate OCR result is correct

purpose: Score the correctness (0 to 1) of an OCR result for a text, formula or table region given the region image, so reliable regions are auto-accepted, the rest go to human review, or the best of several OCR outputs is picked (card).

license.name: Apache-2.0 (card tag)
license.notes: Card tag apache-2.0; no LICENSE file in the repo listing.

architecture.kind: Qwen3.5-2B vision-language with a binary classification head (single_label_classification)

pc-12gb.notes: 4.43 GB against a VRAM budget of 9.6 GB (VRAM minus about 2.4 GB), KV cache not included

pc-16gb.notes: 4.43 GB against a VRAM budget of 13.6 GB (VRAM minus about 2.4 GB), KV cache not included

pc-24gb.notes: 4.43 GB against a VRAM budget of 21.6 GB (VRAM minus about 2.4 GB), KV cache not included

pc-32gb.notes: 4.43 GB against a VRAM budget of 29.6 GB (VRAM minus about 2.4 GB), KV cache not included

mac-16-24gb.notes: 4.43 GB against a GPU share of about 12 GB (KV cache not included)

mac-32gb.notes: 4.43 GB against a GPU share of about 22 GB (KV cache not included)

mac-64gb+.notes: 4.43 GB against a GPU share of about 52 GB (KV cache not included)

other: OpenBMB SDK service and Docker image with a built-in renderer
engine_support.notes: Input includes a rendering of the candidate text; the plain service needs the caller to supply it.

benchmarks.name: AUROC x100 on parses from MiniCPM-OCR 1.0, GLM-OCR, PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 and Xiaomi-OCR-0

strengths: a verifier that works across different OCR engines
weaknesses: needs a candidate OCR result and the region category as input, so it is a pipeline add-on, not a parser
best_for: confidence gating of an OCR pipeline (auto-accept versus review)
soft.maturity: 71.7k downloads, 99 likes; benchmark JevOCRBench published by the same lab

tona_fit.reason: A useful quality gate for a document pipeline (decide which pages need a second pass), but it presupposes a parser and a region-level pipeline; revisit when Tona offers document parsing.
blockers: needs region crops and a renderer
no Tona path for the classification head

open_questions: German or other-language performance (card lists English and Chinese)
